principles: Parallel Wave is collection-level scheduling and recovery state, not authority evidence.
Canonical Story remains the per-story truth carrier; wave state references it instead of redefining it.
Capability and degradation must be explicit before dispatch recommendations are shown.
Every command added here must be CLI/JSON stable, read-only or no-overwrite, and registered in policy/fact levels.
Prefer mechanical smoke tests over prose-only acceptance.
drivers: Need accelerate large development by safely parallelizing related stories/worktrees.
Need preserve Lattice authority boundary: local DONE and production DONE remain separate.
Need avoid conflicting with active Lattice v1 productization surfaces already shipping in B-cd31.

options.name: A: Add Lattice Parallel Wave as a collection-level projection
pros: Does not modify Canonical Story v0 schema
Can reference existing stories, capability probes, evidence, and handoff state
cons: Requires one new schema/model and command family
Still requires operators or future runner to execute the plan

options.name: B: Add DAG fields directly to Canonical Story v0
pros: All relationship data travels with each story export
cons: Conflicts with strict v0 schema shape
Makes per-story export carry collection-level concerns
Raises migration risk for existing handoff/evidence smokes

options.name: C: Only improve existing advisory parallel-policy output
cons: Does not provide wave-level execution document, host capability matching, evidence/merge guidance, or reusable artifact

chosen: A: Add Lattice Parallel Wave as a collection-level projection
rationale: A collection-level wave gives the user real multi-story acceleration while preserving Lattice boundaries and avoiding Canonical Story schema drift.

preMortem.scenario: Wave artifact is mistaken for DONE evidence
preMortem.trigger: Command output says ready/done without authority disclaimer
preMortem.consequence: Agent can use scheduling text to overclaim completion
preMortem.mitigation: All outputs include productionDone=false, authorityChanged=false, and command policy/fact level L0 read-only classification.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel plan recommends unsafe concurrent DEV
preMortem.trigger: Dependencies or sharedHotspots are ignored when explicit parallelSafe=yes is present
preMortem.consequence: Agents collide in the same files or implement downstream before upstream
preMortem.mitigation: Wave analysis treats active dependencies and hotspot overlaps as degradations that override unsafe recommendations.

preMortem.trigger: Plan assigns browser/evidence/receipt work to a host with conditional or unavailable capability
preMortem.mitigation: Use capability_probe semantics and emit visible degradations plus fallback/recovery guidance.

preMortem.scenario: New command bypasses Koala process contracts
preMortem.trigger: Handlers are registered but not command-policy/process-fact-levels covered
preMortem.consequence: Owner lease or audit tooling misclassifies new surface
preMortem.mitigation: Update CLI schema, registry, command-policy, process-fact-levels, and smoke assertions together.
